query: Which model-complexity penalties (AIC, BIC, cross-validated log-score) best prevent overfitting when selecting among skewed/heavy-tailed innovation distributions and GARCH variants?

response.query: Which model-complexity penalties (AIC, BIC, cross-validated log-score) best prevent overfitting when selecting among skewed/heavy-tailed innovation distributions and GARCH variants?
response.answer: BIC and cross-validated log-score are best for preventing overfitting in skewed/heavy-tailed distributions and GARCH variants. BIC penalizes model complexity more strictly than AIC. Cross-validation provides a robust assessment of model performance.
